mustNotSay.text: No individual's name, handle, likeness or hint (suspects, victims, founders, investigators). The radar redacted 3 name(s) as "[named person]"; never fill them in or describe who they are. Organisations, protocols and agencies are fine; an official only when a cited law-enforcement or regulator release names them.

Sources state 3 different loss figures (DefiLlama reported loss $6,360,000,000; Chainalysis $6.4 Billion; Chainalysis $6 billion; Decrypt $6.4 billion). Say each with its source; never average, merge or pick a "real" one.

CoinDesk hedges ("potential") in "Binance hackers push $247 million through transactions designed to cloud the source": repeat it only attributed and with the hedge, or leave it out. Never state it as fact.

A source links this to a state or threat group. Name the group only as "according to <source>" in the same sentence, never in a title, thumbnail or on its own. Do not add attributions the sources do not make.
Court, prosecution and freezing items are filings and allegations, not findings: "prosecutors say", "the filing says". Never "guilty", "stole" or "criminal" as our words.

No code, addresses, transaction hashes, function or contract names, payloads or step-by-step attack sequences, on screen or spoken. One or two concept-level sentences for the mechanism. Defensive checklists are fine.
No prices, token moves, market talk, "buy/sell/hold", returns or income claims. "Price oracle" as a mechanism name is fine.
No "probably", "likely", "rumoured", "insiders say", "must have been", or question headlines about causes. Only what the sources confirm.
No screenshots, redrawn charts, logos or images of other people's posts or dashboards. Describe the finding and attribute it.
Aggregators (Web3 is Going Just Great, crypto.news) never carry a claim or a figure alone; cite a tier-A or tier-B source for it.

policy: Candidates are the radar's top and also-seen incidents, best score first.

A daily Short needs all of: confirmed status; the radar's sourcing check (2 or more independent sources, a mechanism a source states, a strong evergreen fix); no approved episode about the same incident (same radar id, or the same protocol within 3 days) in the last 14 days; and at least one strong analysis that is not a daily template: a pattern from our own radar history (3 or more same-type incidents in 7 or more daily radar files), or a Solana fund-flow trace from published addresses. The DefiLlama 30-day comparison and the side-by-side figures are templates: they may support a real analysis, never replace it.
An explained disagreement between sources (a source says why the figures differ) is real analysis too, but only a person can find that explanation: the owner can pick such a story by hand.
The primary is the best-scoring eligible incident; the alternates are the next two eligible ones.
If nothing is eligible, there is no video today. Developing stories are listed for the owner but never picked automatically (a "what we know" Short needs his call: prepare --pick <id>).
Only one daily video per day: once a video for the date is approved, prepare picks nothing new unless --pick is given.
